# Is the sampling budget worth it?

I re-read the abstract and I am not sure we should drop it. If this holds for our benchmark, sampling and voting beats a single greedy chain:

> self-consistency boosts the performance of chain-of-thought prompting with a striking margin

[wang2022selfconsistency, p. 1](labshelf:wang2022selfconsistency#p1)
:::

::: {#n-G0BPEWJT2AJT2AJT25HDSG0GVF .labshelf-item author="Bruno" created="2026-10-21T11:30:00.000Z"}
It holds on arithmetic, but we pay for every sample. Ten paths is ten times the tokens, and our budget is fixed.
:::

::: {#n-K71KR8R8R8R8R3QVFK7BZ3QVFK .labshelf-item author="Ana" created="2026-10-21T15:02:00.000Z"}
Fair. What if we test it on the 200-question dev set with 5 paths and compare cost per correct answer?
:::

::: {#n-7BZ3JT258R8K7BT2AJT2ADSN1X .labshelf-item author="Bruno" created="2026-10-22T08:47:00.000Z"}
I can run that, but someone has to say which prompt we fix. I would keep the chain-of-thought exemplars from the first paper unchanged.
:::
